transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-05-01 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Redwood CSM); Marta Ruiz (Everleaf VP Eng), Devon Lin (Everleaf SRE), Sydney Park (Everleaf PM), Omar Hadi (Everleaf Security)

Summary: quick handoff from sales to success/engineering. Align pilot scope, security checklist, and immediate deliverables. High-level discussion of Dedicated vs Hosted pilot, benchmarking needs, and integration touchpoints (SSO, VPC, KMS).

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. This is Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick around-the-room — who wants to start?
[00:10] Marta: Hi, Marta here. VP of Eng at Everleaf. We're excited, looking to replace a mix of in-house models and an expensive vendor for product search and support summarization.
[00:22] Devon: Devon — principal SRE. I'm here for infra constraints, networking, perf.
[00:28] Sydney: Sydney, PM for AI initiatives, will own pilot success criteria.
[00:33] Omar: Omar, security. I will review compliance and keys.
[00:38] Jordan: Great. From Redwood Priya is our SE and Alex will run success ops. Priya, want to walk through proposed pilot outline?
[00:45] Priya: Yeah sure. So our recommendation is a 3-week pilot with a small Dedicated pool — think 2x A100-equivalent instances — to get stable latency numbers under your production-like workload. We'll run 1) latency & throughput benchmarks, 2) quality/regression checks against your prompt set, and 3) integration tests for SSO and data routing. The goal is to validate P99 < 300ms for search completions at your peak qps and keep token cost under the threshold you set.
[01:20] Marta: P99 < 300ms is aggressive for our longer contexts, are you planning quantization? Or will this be full fp16?
[01:28] Priya: Good question. For the pilot we'll evaluate multiple runtimes: fp16 baseline and a quantized int8 pathway. The runtime supports quant-friendly kernels; sometimes quantization saves cost with small latency tradeoffs, other times it actually helps latency due to reduced memory pressure. We'll measure both.
[01:45] Devon: On infra — we run a private VPC in GCP. We need to understand networking: will Redwood deploy inside our VPC or do we use a private endpoint? How does traffic egress work?
[01:58] Alex: Alex here — we support both Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) and a VPC peering/private endpoint model for Redwood-hosted. For the pilot we usually recommend private endpoint to speed onboarding; if you need an air-gapped on-prem install that's a later step.
[02:15] Omar: From security perspective we need SOC 2 report, SAML SSO, and customer-managed KMS for key wrapping. Also audit log retention and ability to redact logs.
[02:28] Jordan: We'll make that part of the handoff; Alex will send SOC 2 docs and the SSO/KMS checklist.
[02:35] Alex: I'll share a one-pager for SSO + KMS options. Quick note — we offer two KMS integrations: managed via our cloud partner or bring-your-own-key via customer KMS with HSM-backed wrapping. If you need HSM-backed attestations we can map that out.
[02:52] Devon: When you say "bring-your-own-key" — does Redwood ever see plaintext model inputs or tokens? We need to know data residency and access.
[03:05] Priya: We don't persist raw customer payloads in the hosted flow unless you opt in for debugging. With Private deployment, you control network egress and logs; we can configure redaction and retention. We'll include the specifics in the security doc.
[03:22] Marta: Ok. On success criteria — Sydney and I sketched SLOs: P99 latency target, average cost per 1k tokens, and a human evaluation score where summarization must beat baseline by 5% on a rubric. We want those validated in the pilot.
[03:40] Sydney: Also interested in rollback/rollout model — if we pin a model and then need a fallback what's the process?
[03:47] Priya: The platform supports model pinning and automatic fallback to a compatible variant. For example, if the fp16 variant fails or we see high latency, we can route to a smaller quantized variant. We can demonstrate this in canary rollouts during the pilot.
[04:05] Jordan: Budget question — we discussed earlier your procurement threshold. We proposed Dedicated for production but pilot pricing can be hosted with reserved burst. Devon, Marta, any procurement constraints?
[04:18] Marta: We have an approval window next quarter. For pilot we prefer a low-friction path — hosted pilot to validate quality, then move to Dedicated if perf warrant. But if Dedicated is materially cheaper at production scale that's good to know.
[04:32] Devon: We want to test under real spike scenarios. If pilot lives on hosted but uses a private endpoint, it might not reproduce your peak network characteristics.
[04:42] Priya: We can run the performance benchmarks from within your VPC using Redwood's private endpoint option — that'll exercise the same network path.
[04:50] Omar: Also need to know token retention: can you purge logs on demand? We have GDPR-ish requirements and a right-to-be-forgotten flow.
[04:59] Alex: Yes — per-customer retention settings. We can also exclude storing user prompts by default. I'll include retention options in the doc.
[05:10] Speaker 1: [inaudible] ...sorry can you repeat that last bit?
[05:15] Jordan: Sure — Alex will send retention options and SOC 2.
[05:18] Priya: For the benchmark plan we'll need: a) traffic sample (qps over 7 days), b) sample prompts including long contexts, c) target accuracy metric. Devon, Sydney can you provide those?
[05:30] Devon: Yes, we can export logs — there may be PII so we'll scrub. We'll deliver a CSV with timestamped requests and seq length distribution.
[05:40] Sydney: We'll also add the rubric for summarization scoring. Might take a couple days to align with stakeholders.
[05:46] Jordan: Great. Let's talk timeline — we'd like to kick pilot mid-May if we can collect artifacts early week of May 4. Does that work?
[05:56] Marta: That timing should be fine. Procurement might want a statement of work; Jordan, can you provide a short SOW for the pilot?
[06:04] Jordan: Yes — a one-pager SOW with objectives, scope, and timebox. I'll attach it to the pricing worksheet.
[06:10] Omar: On the SSO front — we use Okta. We need SP metadata and an SP-initiated flow. Can Redwood's console support Just-In-Time provisioning and SCIM?
[06:22] Alex: We support SAML SSO with SP metadata and SAML-based provisioning. SCIM is available for larger customers; we can include SCIM if you want user provisioning automated.
[06:33] Omar: Also we'd like to ensure RBAC mappings so only certain users can deploy models.
[06:38] Priya: RBAC model supports role-based permissions (Admin, DevOps, Viewer, Auditor). We'll walk through mapping during the onboarding session.
[06:47] Devon: A technical question — how do you handle KV cache across rolling updates? We can't have cold-starts blow up latency.
[06:55] Priya: Runtime keeps persistent KV cache per session where possible; during rolling updates we support warm-up and shard-aware cache priming. For the pilot we'll instrument cache hit metrics and simulate rolling updates.
[07:12] Jordan: Let's move to integration tasks — network, keys, and access. Alex?
[07:17] Alex: I'll drop a checklist: SSO metadata, KMS ARN and key policy, VPC endpoint IP ranges, CIDR allowlist, and the audit log retention preference. Also an onboarding calendar with a 2-hour technical deep-dive (SE-led) and a 1-hour ops kickoff.
[07:33] Marta: Good. On governance, we'll want to see how you surface quality regressions — is there a way to tie prompt sets to alerts?
[07:42] Priya: Yes — Redwood Optimize offers evals tied to prompt sets. You can set thresholds and get regression alerts if quality drops after a model change. We'll demo that.
[07:55] Sydney: Is there a metrics dashboard template we can reuse? We don't want to build dashboards from scratch.
[08:01] Alex: We have per-route and per-model dashboards with token cost, latency percentiles, and error rates. We can share a starter dashboard and a Grafana exporter if you prefer self-hosted metrics.
[08:13] Devon: Regarding data residency — our EU users mandate regional processing. Can you pin inference to EU zones?
[08:20] Priya: Yes — routing policies can pin by region, and we can pin model variants to run in EU region only. That will be in the deployment config.
[08:30] Omar: A quick ask: can the platform redact embeddings or any derived vector stores if needed?
[08:36] Priya: Embeddings are generated but storage is optional. If you push to your vector DB we never see it unless you route through our managed caching. We can also configure on-write redaction and retention.
[08:50] Jordan: A couple of tradeoff questions we commonly see — cost vs latency and batching vs per-request latency. Devon, what's your tolerance for batching?
[08:59] Devon: We can accept modest batching if P99 doesn't spike. For search, users are sensitive to latency; for async summarization we can tolerate higher latency.
[09:09] Priya: Perfect. We'll craft two profiles: a low-latency profile with constrained batch sizes and a cost-optimized config using continuous batching and caching. We'll include expected token-cost estimates per profile.
[09:24] Speaker 2: [background noise] ...
[09:28] Jordan: All right — let's capture immediate deliverables. Alex, Priya, Jordan will prepare pilot SOW, pricing, and benchmark plan. Everleaf to deliver traffic sample, prompts, and rubric.
[09:40] Alex: I'll send docs by 2026-05-06.
[09:44] Devon: We'll aim to have the CSV and distribution by 2026-05-04, though might be a day or two depending on approvals.
[09:52] Sydney: I'll finalize success criteria by 2026-05-07.
[09:56] Marta: One more question — if we need private deployment later, what's the expected lead time?
[10:03] Priya: For on-prem fully air-gapped install it's typically 8-12 weeks due to packaging and validation. VPC/private endpoint is much faster, usually 1-2 weeks to configure.
[10:14] Omar: Any upfront security assessments required for Dedicated?
[10:18] Alex: We do a security questionnaire and network review; we can run that in parallel with pilot admin tasks.
[10:25] Jordan: Nice. Anything else?
[10:28] Marta: No, seems covered. Thanks everyone.
[10:31] Jordan: Quick recap — action items recorded. We'll circulate SOW, pricing, SOC2 and SSO/KMS checklist. Pilot kickoff targeted mid-May. Meeting adjourned.
[10:46] End of call
